practices.practice: Read the MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable at runtime and store production credentials in a secrets store such as Azure Key Vault instead of committing them.
practices.prior_belief: Read the MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or commit credentials. Use a secrets store (Azure Key Vault) in production to supply that URI.
practices.source_name: Secure your Azure Key Vault secrets
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string Key Vault

practices.practice: Create a single shared MongoClient/Mongoose connection per process (singleton) and reuse it rather than opening a client per request, sizing the connection pool according to expected concurrency.
practices.prior_belief: Open a single shared Mongoose/MongoDB client (connection pool) per Node process and reuse it; configure pool options such as maxPoolSize (e.g. 50) and socketTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS rather than creating new connections per request.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB tutorial mongoose connection reuse

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS enabled and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS in the connection string (mongodb+srv or tls=true) and ensure server certificate validation is not disabled in production.
practices.source_name: Security — Azure DocumentDB (transport security / TLS)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TLS required tls=true

practices.practice: Create compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range); for history queries prefer { customerId: 1, timestamp: -1 } and { channel: 1, timestamp: -1 } to serve equality + recent-first sorts.
practices.prior_belief: Create compound indexes with equality fields first, then sort/range fields. For history queries create indexes exactly: { customerId: 1, timestamp: -1 } and { channel: 1, timestamp: -1 } (timestamp descending supports recent-first).
practices.source_name: Indexing Strategies — Azure DocumentDB (compound index / ESR)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB compound index ESR best practices

practices.practice: For large-offset pagination avoid skip-based paging; use cursor (keyset) pagination using your compound index (e.g., timestamp desc, _id tie-breaker) and return an opaque resume token.
practices.prior_belief: Do not rely on skip-based pagination for large offsets; implement cursor-based pagination using the compound index (e.g. query customerId = X AND (timestamp < lastTimestamp OR (timestamp = lastTimestamp AND _id < lastId)) sorted by timestamp desc, _id desc) and return an opaque nextCursor token.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB pagination skip vs cursor Mongoose tutorial

practices.practice: Make seed/import scripts idempotent by using upsert operations (updateOne / replaceOne with upsert: true or bulkWrite with upsert) to avoid duplicate documents on repeated runs.
practices.prior_belief: Make seeding idempotent by using updateOne(..., { upsert: true }) or bulkWrite with upsert operations and a unique key (e.g. externalInteractionId or a deterministic _id) to avoid duplicates on repeated runs.
practices.source_name: Updating data in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (update / upsert examples)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB updateOne upsert example

practices.practice: Store timestamps as Date/ISODate (UTC) values (ISO 8601 with Z) and index the timestamp field to support time-range queries.
practices.prior_belief: Validate and store timestamps in UTC ISODate (JavaScript Date) and index the timestamp field; never store local-time strings for time-range queries.
practices.source_name: Date operators and examples (ISODate usage)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB ISODate UTC examples

practices.practice: Use database-side JSON Schema validators or application schemas (Mongoose schemas) to enforce required fields and basic structure to prevent schema drift in multi-channel single collections.
practices.prior_belief: Use a JSON Schema / collection validator or Mongoose schema to enforce required fields (customerId, channel, timestamp, content/embedding) at write time to prevent schema drift in a single collection storing multiple channel types.
practices.source_name: $jsonSchema (validation) — Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB JSON Schema validator $jsonSchema

practices.practice: Disable automatic Mongoose index creation (autoIndex: false) in production and create indexes explicitly during deployment or in an idempotent migration step.
practices.prior_belief: Disable Mongoose/MongoDB autoIndex in production (autoIndex: false) and create indexes explicitly during deployment or as an idempotent migration script to avoid runtime indexing overhead.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API (index creation guidance)
practices.how_found: Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB disable autoIndex guidance

practices.practice: When using vector/embedding fields, store vectors as number[] and create a matching cosmosSearch vector index with the correct dimensions and similarity; mismatched dimensions or similarity settings produce silently incorrect results.
practices.prior_belief: When using vector fields/embeddings, store vectors as an array of numbers of the expected dimensionality and create the cluster vector index with matching dimension and index type (HNSW/IVF) — validate vector length on write to match index configuration.
practices.source_name: Index vector data in Cosmos DB (vector-search guidance)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index dimensions must match embeddings

practices.practice: If only a subset of documents contain a field such as an embedding, use partial or sparse indexes to avoid indexing lots of empty/unused values (createIndex with partialFilterExpression where supported).
practices.prior_belief: Use partial indexes or sparse indexes if only a subset of documents contain a field (e.g. embedding) to avoid indexing large unused fields: e.g. createIndex({ embedding: 'vector' }, { partialFilterExpression: { embedding: { $exists: true } } }) where supported.
practices.source_name: Index types and index properties — Azure DocumentDB (partial / sparse indexes supported)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB partial index partialFilterExpression support

practices.practice: Handle rate limits and transient errors by implementing retries with exponential backoff and jitter, honoring the service's retry headers (x-ms-retry-after-ms / Retry-After) and recognizing SDK/server-side retry behavior.
practices.prior_belief: Protect against rate-limiting (429) and transient network errors by implementing retries with exponential backoff and jitter; read Retry-After/Retry-After-ms when available and back off accordingly.
practices.source_name: Diagnose and troubleshoot "Request rate too large" (429) exceptions
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB 429 retry x-ms-retry-after-ms guidance

practices.practice: Keep documents small and avoid embedding large binary blobs; store attachments in blob/object storage and keep references in documents to reduce RU cost and indexing overhead.
practices.prior_belief: Keep documents small — avoid embedding large blobs (images/audio). If attachments are needed, store them in blob/object storage and keep only references in the document; aim to stay well under typical document size limits (MongoDB 16MB guidance).
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB document size 16 MB guidance and best practices

practices.practice: Project only required fields in queries and aggregations to lower RU consumption and network payloads.
practices.prior_belief: Use projection (select only needed fields) on queries and aggregations to reduce RU consumption and network payload — e.g. projection { content: 1, timestamp: 1, channel: 1 } for history lists.
practices.source_name: Understand request units consumption in Azure Cosmos DB (projection affects RU)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB projection reduce RU consumption

practices.practice: Monitor RU/s and slow queries (enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs) and use those logs to identify heavy queries and inform index tuning.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s consumption and tune queries and indexes accordingly; use explain() or the MCP tooling to verify query plans use the intended compound indexes and to measure RU charge for representative queries.
practices.source_name: Monitor Azure DocumentDB diagnostics logs with Azure Monitor / slow-query guidance
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB enable diagnostic settings slow-query logs

practices.practice: Make aggregation endpoints efficient by filtering ($match) on indexed fields first, then using $group / $sort so the pipeline can rely on indexes and avoid full scans.
practices.prior_belief: For aggregation endpoints (channel breakdown), use the aggregation pipeline with $match (indexed fields), then $group and $sort; restrict the match by indexed fields (channel or customerId and time range) so the pipeline is RU-efficient.
practices.source_name: Optimize request cost in Azure Cosmos DB (queries and indexing guidance)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB aggregation pipeline filter on indexed fields then group

practices.practice: Configure sensible client-side timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) so requests fail fast when the cluster is unreachable, and tune pool settings to prevent resource exhaustion.
practices.prior_belief: Implement request-level timeouts and sensible serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS so app requests fail fast if the cluster is unreachable rather than accumulating queued requests occupying the pool.
practices.source_name: documentdb-connection
practices.how_found: load_skill documentdb-connection

practices.practice: Use acknowledged writes and idempotent operations (upsert, dedupe keys, or replace with known id) to make retry-safe behavior predictable and avoid unbounded retries of non-idempotent inserts.
practices.prior_belief: Use acknowledged writes and idempotent operations for retry safety — for example, use upsert or deduplication keys and avoid unbounded retries of non-idempotent inserts.
practices.source_name: Design resilient applications with Azure Cosmos DB SDKs (retry guidance)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB SDK retries idempotent writes guidance

practices.practice: If you need automatic data expiry, enable TTL (time-to-live) via a TTL index (on _ts) or configure a custom TTL field (account capability may be required) and validate the supported semantics.
practices.prior_belief: If you need automatic data expiration, use a TTL index on the timestamp field or container-level TTL where supported to expire old interactions, and verify how TTL is implemented in the MongoDB API of the service.
practices.source_name: Expire data with Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB and per-document TTL
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TTL _ts expireAfterSeconds guidance

practices.practice: Include a lightweight 'channel' discriminator field when storing different channel messages in one collection and design indexes (channel + timestamp) around access patterns rather than scattering many per-channel collections unless access patterns demand separation.
practices.prior_belief: Protect against schema drift in a single collection used by many channels by including a lightweight 'channel' discriminator and consider partial projections or polymorphic subdocuments; plan indexes around queries (channel + timestamp) rather than per-channel collections unless very different access patterns require separation.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API (discriminators / one-collection patterns)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Mongoose discriminators single collection best practice

practices.practice: Run explain() / executionStats for representative queries during development to confirm that intended indexes are used and to detect COLLSCANs.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() for sample queries during development to confirm the created compound indexes are being used and to detect COLLSCANs; examine index keys, numberExamined, and RU or time cost.
practices.source_name: Indexing Strategies — Azure DocumentDB (compound index / explain example)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB explain executionStats index usage

practices.practice: Avoid creating overly broad wildcard indexes; limit indexing to the fields that match your query patterns (customerId, channel, timestamp, embedding when used) to conserve RU and storage.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid creating overly broad wildcard indexes; only index fields that support the query patterns (customerId, channel, timestamp, embedding (vector) when used), to conserve RU and storage.
practices.source_name: Manage indexing in Azure DocumentDB (wildcard / index budget guidance)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB wildcard index costs and index budget

practices.practice: Scale container throughput (or enable autoscale) for heavy aggregation or read workloads to avoid throttling, and use driver-side maxTimeMS (per-query) to bound long-running queries.
practices.prior_belief: When running aggregation or heavy read workloads, consider scaling RU/s (or enabling autoscale) for the container to prevent throttling, and set a reasonable maxTimeMS for queries to avoid runaway queries that waste RU.
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB service limits and query execution guidance
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB scale RU autoscale and maxTimeMS guidance

practices.practice: Make index creation idempotent in setup scripts (createIndexes) and avoid dropping/recreating indexes in production unless necessary; issue index builds non-blocking when adding to large historical data sets.
practices.prior_belief: Make index creation idempotent in setup scripts (createIndexes or ensureIndex) and avoid dropping and recreating indexes in production unless necessary; run index creation during a maintenance window if it impacts RU.
practices.source_name: Indexing Best Practices in Azure DocumentDB (createIndex guidance)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB createIndex non-blocking and idempotent guidance

practices.practice: Return minimal error details to callers (avoid leaking secrets or internals) while logging full diagnostics (stack, query plan, RU charge) to protected logs/monitoring only.
practices.prior_belief: Return minimal error details to callers (avoid leaking connection strings or internal diagnostics); log rich diagnostics (stack, query plan, RU charge) to trusted logs/monitoring only.
practices.source_name: Best practices for monitoring and diagnostics (don't log secrets / scrub logs)
practices.how_found: Azure monitoring best practices don't log secrets guidance
